_manual_start: Docker Desktop (it does not start by itself after a reboot) - needed for Tasks 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15.

Jenkins and the local registry: `cd deploy\jenkins; docker compose up -d`, then wait about 1 minute for http://localhost:8090 (user `admin`; the password is the JENKINS_ADMIN_PASSWORD line in deploy/jenkins/.env - never show that file).
Staging (port 8081) is recreated by running the Jenkins job once: open http://localhost:8090/job/hotel-booking/build?delay=0sec and click Build (about 90 seconds).
For Tasks 13 and 14: `cd deploy\ansible\lab; docker compose up -d target`, wait about 25 seconds. It answers on http://localhost:8088.
Close other windows that could cover the screen and do not touch the mouse while re-recording: recordings capture one window only, but a window on top of it would be captured too.

Ports used: 5000 (registry; also used for a few seconds by the Task 3 demo app, so stop the registry first if you re-record Task 3), 8081 (staging), 8082 (prod), 8088 (Ansible lab), 8090 (Jenkins), 18000 (Task 11 demo container).
_findings: docs/04-git-workflow.md ('Honest status of GitHub'), docs/pull-requests/README.md and docs/08-project-report.md (section 6, 'Known limitations') still say the repository was not pushed to GitHub. It was pushed on 2026-10-12 (public repo, 19 branches, tags v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 - confirmed live in the Task 4 video). Only issues and pull requests are missing. I did not edit those documents.

Those documents also quote commit IDs from before the 2026-10-12 history rewrite (for example 8728b62, 37a4663). Current IDs differ; docs/evidence/git/commit-id-map.md maps old to new. The Task 5, 6 and 10 videos use live Git queries and branch names instead.
GitHub still has 0 issues and 0 pull requests (checked live in the Task 2 and Task 5 videos). Creating them needs your GitHub login.
Docker Hub publishing was never tested; only the local registry (localhost:5000) was used. Nothing was published externally and no credential was stored.
The Ansible target is a privileged Ubuntu 24.04 Docker container acting as a server, not a separate VM.
The project is Python: Maven/Tomcat are not used. Whether Maven is mandatory is still a question for the professor.
Jenkins reports builds #2 and #9 as failed on purpose (Task 10 defect experiments). Their Stage View shows later stages in red; Jenkins' own log text for them is 'skipped due to earlier failure(s)'.

The recorder had two bugs that I found and fixed while recording (a variable name clash that broke the first Task 5 recording, and black frames from GPU-rendered Chrome in the first browser recording). Both bad recordings were discarded and redone; none of them is in the pack.
_environment: Windows 11 laptop. ffmpeg 9.0.2 captures one window per recording; the voice-over is a synthetic Windows text-to-speech voice (Microsoft David), not a human voice. Subtitles (.srt) match the voice-over.

Docker Desktop was stopped at the start of the session; I started it. Jenkins, the registry and the staging, prod and Ansible lab containers had been stopped for 7 days; I started Jenkins, the registry and the lab target. They are still running.

I started a real Jenkins build #12 of branch develop (APP_ENV=staging, same commit as build #11) during the Task 8 recording. It succeeded and recreated the staging containers (same version and commit as before).
Task 13 and 14 run Ansible against the lab server: Task 13 updates it to the current working copy; Task 14 deploys a pretend release 1.1.1-demo and rolls it back to 1.1.0 (the lab ends on 1.1.0).
Files I created outside the demonstrations folder: reports/e2e-demo.xml (a JUnit report from the Task 9 demo; the reports/ folder is git-ignored). Temporary folders in %TEMP% were removed after use.

Git: branch feature/ui-redesign, working tree clean apart from the new, untracked folder docs/task-reports/demonstrations/. Nothing was committed, pushed or tagged. No branch, tag or history was changed.
